title: Unveiling Interface Defects and Dislocations in Epitaxial Superconducting Nitrides with Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: One of the main sources of losses in superconducting nitride-based quantum devices arise from nanoscale defects, amorphous dielectrics, contaminants, impurities, and lattice mismatches [1]. Naturally, the interface between two different materials is a prolific host for various dislocations and defects, with columnar structures often forming from these dislocation cores [2]. It is therefore essential to characterize the microscopic structure of devices to devise growth and fabrication processes that minimize undesirable effects.
